q: What is the flower carpet laid out in front of homes during Onam called?
note: Families add a new ring of flowers each day across Onam's ten days.

q: Aranmula kannadi, Kerala's famous handmade mirror, is made from what?
note: The exact alloy recipe is a closely guarded secret of a few artisan families.

q: The Kannada script is most closely related to which other Indian script?
note: Both scripts grew out of the old Telugu-Kannada script of medieval times.

q: Qubani ka meetha, a Hyderabadi wedding dessert, is made from which dried fruit?
note: It is often served topped with fresh cream or custard.

q: Hyderabad's pathar ka gosht is cooked on what?
note: 'Pathar' means stone; the meat sears on granite heated over coals.

q: Which Carnatic legend, born in Sankaraguptam in Andhra Pradesh, created several new ragas?
note: He gave his first full-length concert at the age of eight.

q: Cheriyal scroll paintings, used by travelling storytellers, are a traditional craft of which state?
note: A single Cheriyal scroll can stretch many metres to tell a whole story.

q: What does the tyre brand MRF's name originally stand for?
note: MRF began in 1946 as a small maker of toy balloons in Chennai.

q: Which Kerala classical dance's name means 'dance of the enchantress'?
note: Dancers wear a white-and-gold kasavu costume with jasmine in their hair.

q: Avakaya, Andhra's famous fiery pickle, is made mainly from what?
note: It is made with chopped raw mango, mustard powder, chilli powder and sesame oil.

q: The Mahamastakabhisheka, held about every 12 years at Shravanabelagola, anoints which giant monolithic statue?
note: The statue, carved from a single granite rock, is about 57 feet tall.

q: Madras Day, marking the 1639 land grant to the East India Company that grew into modern Chennai, is celebrated on which date?
note: Heritage enthusiasts in Chennai began celebrating it in 2004.

q: The swaying, bobble-headed 'Thalaiyatti Bommai' dolls are a famous craft of which Tamil Nadu town?
note: The doll's rounded base keeps it bouncing back upright when pushed.

q: In which year was Madras officially renamed Chennai?
note: The name Chennai is linked to the older settlement of Chennapattanam.

q: Puducherry's old French colonial quarter is popularly called what?
note: Its streets still carry French names like Rue Dumas and Rue Suffren.

q: Which giant cantilevered nets are an iconic sight along the shore of Fort Kochi?
note: They are traditionally believed to have been brought by Chinese traders centuries ago.

q: Which Malayalam writer was affectionately called the 'Beypore Sultan'?
note: His comic novel 'Pathummayude Aadu' is about his sister's goat.

q: Ambur, famous for its own style of biryani, is also a big hub for which industry?
note: Ambur biryani is usually made with short-grain seeraga samba rice.

q: What is the golden, globe-shaped meditation hall at the centre of Auroville called?
note: Inside is a large crystal globe lit by a single beam of sunlight.

q: Bandar laddu takes its name from the old name of which Andhra port town?
note: Bandar laddu, made from gram flour and jaggery, has a GI tag.

q: Which Mysuru-born cartoonist created 'The Common Man'?
note: The Common Man appeared in his 'You Said It' strip in The Times of India.

q: Which Hyderabad museum is famous for the marble 'Veiled Rebecca' statue?
note: It also has a musical clock whose tiny figure strikes the hour.

q: Which Hyderabad palace complex, whose name means 'four palaces', was the seat of the Nizams?
note: A vintage Rolls-Royce of the Nizams is displayed there.

q: Which sour leafy green gives its name to one of Andhra's best-loved pickles?
note: Gongura pachadi and gongura mutton are both Andhra classics.

q: Theyyam, the ritual art with towering headgear and red face paint, is mainly performed in which region of Kerala?
note: Theyyam season in North Kerala runs roughly from October to May.

q: In kori rotti, the Mangaluru favourite, 'kori' means chicken in which language?
note: The 'rotti' is a crisp, paper-thin dried rice wafer soaked in the curry.

q: In which year was Pondicherry officially renamed Puducherry?
note: 'Puducherry' means 'new town' in Tamil.

q: Former President A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was born in which island town of Tamil Nadu?
note: As a boy, Kalam helped his family by distributing newspapers.

q: Which Hyderabad lake has a giant monolithic Buddha statue standing in the middle?
note: The lake was built in the 1560s, during Qutb Shahi rule.

q: Srivilliputhur in Tamil Nadu holds a GI tag for which milk sweet?

q: In Hyderabadi Dakhni slang, what does 'nakko' mean?

q: Which caves in Wayanad hold ancient rock engravings of human and animal figures?
note: The caves are really a huge rock cleft formed by a split boulder.

q: Which Karnataka rice-and-lentil dish has a name that literally means 'hot lentil rice'?
note: It is traditionally served with crunchy boondi or potato chips.

q: Which contemporary art festival, first held in 2012, takes place in Kochi?
note: It is named after Muziris, an ancient port that traded with Rome.

q: In Telugu, what does the question 'bagunnara?' ask?

q: Davangere in Karnataka is famous for which butter-laden dosa?

q: On which day of the Pongal festival are cattle decorated and honoured?

q: Which Bengaluru botanical garden holds a famous flower show in its glass house around Independence Day?

q: Rani Abbakka Chowta of Ullal is famous for resisting which European power?

q: Mysore Sandal Soap was first made in which year?

q: Which queen of a small Karnataka kingdom led an armed rebellion against the British in 1824?

q: Which Hampi temple is famous for its stone chariot and musical pillars?
note: The stone chariot appears on the back of the new 50-rupee note.

q: Which chilled drink of milk, almond gum and ice cream is a signature of Madurai?
note: The name is often translated as 'cool heart'.

q: Warangal was the capital of which medieval dynasty?
note: The carved stone Kala Thoranam gateways still stand at Warangal Fort.

q: Which language, closely related to Maldivian Dhivehi, is spoken on Minicoy island?

q: Who was the seventh and last ruling Nizam of Hyderabad?

q: The 1980s TV series 'Malgudi Days' was largely filmed in which Karnataka village?

q: What are Kerala's long racing snake boats called in Malayalam?
note: A snake boat can be over 30 metres long and carry about 100 rowers.

q: Mahe, a part of the union territory of Puducherry, is surrounded by which state?
note: Mahe sits on the Malabar coast between Kerala's Kannur and Kozhikode districts.

q: Which Tamil word is used as a respectful greeting, much like namaste?
note: It is said with palms pressed together, just like namaste.

q: Which Tamil poet-patriot, born in Ettayapuram, is fondly called 'Mahakavi'?

q: Which gorge and fort in Andhra Pradesh is nicknamed the 'Grand Canyon of India'?

q: Which Karnataka hill district is nicknamed the 'Scotland of India'?

q: Which decommissioned submarine is now a museum on Visakhapatnam's RK Beach?
note: It served the Indian Navy for 31 years before becoming a museum in 2002.

q: Which Andhra village is famous for lacquered wooden toys coloured with natural dyes?

q: Bengaluru's metro rail system is popularly called what?

q: Which Andhra port city is nicknamed the 'City of Destiny'?

q: Guntur in Andhra Pradesh is famous for which fiery crop?

q: Which 15th-century Telugu composer from Tallapaka wrote thousands of songs on Lord Venkateswara?
note: Many of his songs were preserved on engraved copper plates.

q: India's Engineers' Day on 15 September marks the birthday of which Karnataka-born engineer?
note: He received the Bharat Ratna in 1955.

q: The Nehru Trophy snake boat race is held on which lake at Alappuzha?

q: Chola bronzes famously show Shiva as the cosmic dancer. What is this form called?

q: Which Tamil Nadu street dish is shredded parotta tossed with egg or salna on a hot griddle?

q: Which 13th-century queen ruled from Warangal after succeeding her father Ganapatideva?
note: Marco Polo praised the diamonds and fine cloth of her kingdom.

q: The temple at Lepakshi in Andhra Pradesh is famous for which unusual pillar?
note: Visitors slide a cloth under it to show it barely touches the floor.

q: Which Tamil Nadu city is nicknamed the 'Manchester of South India' for its textile mills?
note: Coimbatore is also a major hub for pumps and motors.

q: Which Sanskrit theatre form of Kerala was among UNESCO's first proclaimed intangible heritage masterpieces in 2001?
note: A single play could traditionally be performed over many days.

q: Which Kerala martial art is trained in a special pit-like arena called a kalari?
note: Its weapons include the urumi, a flexible sword that bends like a whip.

q: Which freedom fighter, called 'Kappalottiya Thamizhan', launched a Swadeshi shipping company in 1906?
note: His Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company ran ships from Thoothukudi to Colombo.

q: Which satirical Kerala performance art was created by the 18th-century poet Kunchan Nambiar?
note: Legend says Nambiar invented it after being mocked for dozing off during a performance.

q: During Onam, Thrissur's streets fill with performers painted as tigers. What is this folk art called?
note: Performers paint their bellies into tiger faces and shake them to the drumbeat.

q: Which pharma company, founded by K. Anji Reddy in 1984, is headquartered in Hyderabad?
note: Anji Reddy began his career at a state-run drug company before starting his own.

q: If a Kannada speaker asks 'oota aytha?', what do they want to know?
note: 'Oota' means a meal, and asking this is a warm everyday greeting.

q: Telangana's Ramappa Temple is unusually named after whom?
note: Its bricks are said to be so light that they float on water.

q: Thalassery biryani is made with which short-grain fragrant rice instead of basmati?
note: Kaima rice is also called jeerakasala, as its grains look like cumin seeds.

q: In Kerala, what is 'kappa', often eaten with spicy fish curry?

q: The Neelakurinji shrub that turns Munnar's hills blue flowers once every how many years?

q: The Mahamaham festival, held once every 12 years, takes place in which Tamil Nadu town?

q: Which Tamil Nadu hill station is known as the 'Princess of Hill Stations'?
note: Kodaikanal's star-shaped lake was created in 1863.

q: Mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan was born in which Tamil Nadu town?
note: He was born at his maternal grandparents' home in 1887.

q: Which Andhra town gives its name to the block-printed style of Kalamkari?
note: Most of the block printing is now done in nearby Pedana.

q: Which Tamil Nadu town is famous for making fireworks and matchboxes?
note: Sivakasi is also a big centre for printing calendars and diaries.

q: Araku Valley, in the hills near Visakhapatnam, is famous for growing which crop?
note: Araku coffee is grown largely by tribal farmers in the Eastern Ghats.

q: Kerala's cylinder-steamed rice flour and grated coconut dish, often eaten with kadala curry, is called what?
note: It is steamed in a bamboo or steel tube called a puttu kutti.

q: Which 11th-century poet, who began the Telugu Mahabharata, is called the 'Adi Kavi' of Telugu?
note: Tikkana and Errana later completed the Telugu Mahabharata he began.

q: Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh is famous for which crisp fried sweet that bursts with sugar syrup when bitten?
note: Kakinada's version is the hollow, tube-shaped 'gottam kaja'.

q: Kozhikode's famous SM Street, lined with halwa shops, is short for what?
note: Its Malayalam name, Mittai Theruvu, also means sweet street.

q: Nobel-winning physicist C.V. Raman was born near which Tamil Nadu city?
note: Raman was born in 1888 at Thiruvanaikoil, near Tiruchirappalli.

q: In which Karnataka hill district were India's first coffee plants traditionally grown, in the 1600s?
note: Legend says seven coffee beans were smuggled in from Yemen.

q: Which 17th-century British fort in Chennai houses the Tamil Nadu Secretariat?
note: It was the East India Company's first major fortress in India.

q: Hyderabad's IT hub around HITEC City is popularly nicknamed what?
note: HITEC City's landmark Cyber Towers building opened in 1998.

q: Which revolutionary-turned-philosopher founded a famous ashram in Pondicherry in 1926?
note: He moved to Pondicherry in 1910, when it was under French rule.

q: Which chieftain is credited with founding Bengaluru in 1537?
note: Bengaluru's international airport is named after him.

q: Pulasa, a prized seasonal fish from the Godavari, is the local name for which fish?
note: It is caught in the monsoon, when the fish swim upriver from the sea to spawn.

q: Which Indian language is often called the 'Italian of the East'?
note: Like Italian, nearly all Telugu words end in a vowel sound.

q: What does the name 'Lakshadweep' literally mean?
note: Despite the grand name, it has only a few dozen islands.

q: In Bengaluru, 'swalpa adjust maadi' is a friendly request to do what?
note: 'Swalpa' means 'a little' in Kannada.

q: A clap at Golconda Fort's entrance gate can be heard at which hilltop pavilion?
note: The acoustic trick is said to have worked as an early alarm system.

q: In the Mangaluru dish neer dosa, what does 'neer' mean?
note: The batter is so thin and watery that the dosa turns out lacy and soft.

q: Which cotton fabric gets its name from the old Kerala port of Calicut?
note: Calicut's cotton cloth was a prized trade good for European merchants.

q: Which Indian language's name reads the same backwards when written in English?
note: Malayalam has its own letter for the 'zha' sound, as in Kozhikode.

q: Bidriware, blackened metal inlaid with silver, is named after which Karnataka town?
note: Soil from the Bidar fort is used to turn the metal jet black.

q: At Thrissur Pooram, rival temple groups compete by rapidly swapping what atop elephants?
note: This colourful contest is called kudamattam.

q: Hyderabad's twin city Secunderabad is named after which Nizam?
note: Secunderabad began as a British cantonment in 1806.

q: Which 16th-century composer is called the 'Pitamaha', or grandfather, of Carnatic music?
note: He devised graded lessons still used to teach Carnatic music to beginners.

q: Which Tamil Nadu city is nicknamed 'Thoonga Nagaram', the city that never sleeps?
note: Madurai's street food stalls and markets famously stay busy late into the night.

q: In Malayali slang, if something is 'pwoli', it is what?
note: 'Pwoli saanam' is a popular way to call something top-notch.

q: Which poet wrote Karnataka's state song 'Jaya Bharatha Jananiya Tanujate'?
note: Kuvempu was the first Kannada writer to win the Jnanpith Award, in 1967.

q: In Tamil slang, if something is 'semma', it is what?
note: 'Semma mass' is a popular way to hype up something really cool.

q: Which Bengaluru eatery is credited with inventing rava idli during World War II?
note: A wartime rice shortage pushed MTR to try semolina instead.

q: Which queen of Sivaganga fought the British and won back her kingdom in 1780?
note: Tamil people remember her as 'Veeramangai', the brave woman.

q: Which revolutionary led the Rampa Rebellion against the British in 1922-24?
note: He used guerrilla tactics in the forests of the Eastern Ghats.

q: The intricately carved temples of Belur and Halebidu were built by which dynasty?
note: Hoysala sculptors carved in soapstone, which is soft when freshly quarried.

q: Which Kerala city's airport became the world's first fully solar-powered airport in 2015?
note: Cochin airport won the UN's Champions of the Earth award in 2018.

q: Kerala's temple orchestra made up of five kinds of instruments is called what?
note: The five are timila, maddalam, ilathalam, idakka and kombu.

q: The hill town name 'Munnar' refers to the meeting of how many rivers?
note: 'Munnar' literally means 'three rivers'.

q: Vijayawada stands on the banks of which river?
note: The Prakasam Barrage spans the Krishna right at Vijayawada.

q: Lakshadweep's first airport, opened in 1988, is on which island?
note: The runway runs along a narrow strip of the coral island.

q: Badami, famous for its rock-cut cave temples, was known by what name as the Chalukya capital?
note: The cave temples are cut into red sandstone cliffs above Agastya Lake.

q: Aavin is the dairy cooperative brand of which state?
note: Aavin is run by the Tamil Nadu Co-operative Milk Producers' Federation.

q: Which Andhra Pradesh cattle breed became famous in Brazil under the name 'Nelore'?
note: Brazil's Nelore breed is named after Nellore, the district the cattle were shipped from.

q: Which of these is NOT part of the union territory of Puducherry?
note: Yanam lies on the Godavari delta, hundreds of kilometres from Puducherry town.

q: Who founded the Kalakshetra dance and arts academy in Chennai in 1936?
note: Kalakshetra was declared an institution of national importance in 1993.

q: How tall, in feet, is the Thiruvalluvar statue at Kanyakumari?
note: It stands on a small rock islet next to the Vivekananda Rock Memorial.

q: How many letters are traditionally counted in the Tamil alphabet?
note: 12 vowels, 18 consonants, 216 combined letters and one special letter, aytham.

q: Tirunelveli in Tamil Nadu is famous for which glossy wheat-and-ghee sweet?
note: Its halwa is often said to owe its taste to water from the Thamirabarani river.

q: Which Malayalam poet founded the Kerala Kalamandalam arts school in 1930?
note: Kalamandalam sits at Cheruthuruthy on the banks of the Bharathapuzha river.

q: Lakshadweep falls under the jurisdiction of which state's High Court?
note: The islands lie roughly 200 to 440 km off the Kerala coast.

q: Kondapalli's light wooden toys are made in a village near which Andhra city?
note: The toys are carved from a soft local wood called tella poniki.

q: Chennai's famous December music and dance season is named after which Tamil month?
note: Hundreds of Carnatic concerts are held in city sabhas during the season.

q: What is the huge, precariously balanced boulder at Mamallapuram popularly called?
note: Despite sitting on a slope, the boulder has stayed put for centuries.

q: In Malayalam, what do you call your elder sister?
note: An elder brother is 'chettan', often called out as 'chetta'.

q: Which Vijayapura mausoleum is famous for its whispering gallery?
note: A whisper under its huge dome can be heard clearly across the gallery.

q: During Bathukamma, women stack what into tall cone-shaped arrangements before floating them in water?
note: Local flowers like tangedu and gunuka are favourites for the stacks.

q: Silambam, a traditional martial art of Tamil Nadu, is fought mainly with what?
note: Skilled players spin the staff so fast it looks like a blur.

q: Before 1973, Lakshadweep was officially called the Laccadive, Minicoy and which Islands?
note: The new name Lakshadweep took effect on 1 November 1973.

q: Hyderabad's Laad Bazaar, near the Charminar, is famous for which item?
note: It is also called Choodi Bazaar, 'choodi' meaning bangle.

q: The Medaram Jatara, a huge tribal festival held every two years in Telangana, honours whom?
note: Devotees offer jaggery, called 'bangaram' (gold), often equal to their body weight.

q: What are Kerala's traditional thatched rice-barge houseboats called?
note: 'Kettu' means tied: the planks are lashed together with coir rope instead of nails.

q: Which Kerala backwater town is nicknamed the 'Venice of the East'?
note: Its web of canals made houseboat cruises its signature tourist trip.

q: Karimnagar in Telangana is famous for delicate filigree work in which metal?
note: Karimnagar silver filigree has a GI tag.

q: Which salty-sweet biscuit is the classic partner to Hyderabadi Irani chai?
note: Hyderabad's Irani cafes trace back to Persian immigrants of the Nizam era.

q: Which crop is the backbone of farming in Lakshadweep?
note: Copra and coir from coconuts are key local products.

q: Which Hyderabad festival sees women carry decorated pots of cooked rice as offerings in the month of Ashada?
note: 'Bonam' means a meal, offered in a decorated brass or clay pot.
